For every incident with valid coordinate: For every incident with valid coordinates, downloads OpenStreetMap tiles and composes a PNG centered on the incident's location, marked with a dot. The file path is written to the einsatz.kartenbildPfad state, e.g. for sending as a Pushover attachment from a Blockly/JavaScript script. Only the 10 most recent images are kept, older ones are deleted automatically. Uses the public tile.openstreetmap.org server - keep this to the intended one-image-per-incident use per the OSM Tile Usage Policy.

Loaded live from the configured server's: Loaded live from the configured server's /waip/ overview page - choose by Leitstelle, Kreis, Träger or Wache, or pick 'Alle Wachalarme' (ID 0) for every incident. If the server can't be reached, an ID can still be entered manually.
Maps einsatz.stichwort to einsatz.beschr: Maps einsatz.stichwort to einsatz.beschreibung. Comparison is case-insensitive and treats spaces/hyphens as equivalent (any run of either collapses to one before comparing), so e.g. "H:VU mit P" and "H:VU-mit-P" match the same row - no need for a separate row per spelling. If several rows match, the most specific (longest) pattern wins automatically - row order has no effect on matching, sort by any column freely. Pre-filled with an example fire/rescue keyword list as a starting point - it is not confirmed to match your own dispatch center's actual keywords, edit/replace as needed. To back up or transfer this table, use ioBroker's standard instance configuration export/import (JSON). After using that import, reload the Admin page before checking this table - the open config dialog doesn't refresh it from an external import automatically (a state-sync limitation of the Admin table component itself).
When unchecked, incidents whose einsatza: When unchecked, incidents whose einsatzart identifies them as a rescue-service call (contains "Rettung" or "Krankentransport", case-insensitive) are ignored completely - no states are updated, no history entry is written, no TTS announcement is triggered. Useful because some WAIP dispatch centers only ever signal rescue-service incidents unreliably or not at all. Enabled by default to match previous behavior.
Rescue-service keyword scheme R<RTW>N<NE: Rescue-service keyword scheme R<RTW>N<NEF>, optionally followed by a p/f modifier and/or an NT suffix (e.g. "R1N0" = 1 ambulance, no emergency physician). Two spellings are recognized: without a space and with a hyphen before NT (Leitstelle Lausitz, e.g. "R1N1p", "R1N0-NT") and with a space and without a hyphen (Leitstelle Brandenburg/IRLS, e.g. "R1N1 p", "R1N0 nt") - only enable if your dispatch center actually uses one of these patterns. Takes priority over the table on the Keyword descriptions tab when a keyword matches.
